title: Combine two features
summary: One unit can combine several inputs. Multiply each input by its own weight, add the products, then add the bias.
introduction: One unit can combine several inputs. Multiply each input by its own weight, add the products, then add the bias. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: One unit can combine several inputs. Multiply each input by its own weight, add the products, then add the bias.

blocks.code:
inputs = [2, 3]
weights = [4, 1]
bias = 1
value = sum(x * w for x, w in zip(inputs, weights)) + bias
print(value)
blocks.title: Combine two features

blocks.text: The output is 12. The products are 8 and 3, and the bias adds 1. zip pairs each input with its matching weight.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change only the second weight to 2.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Each feature needs the intended matching weight; order matters.
